results.title: Effects of Background Checks on Violent Crime | RAND
results.content: # Effects of Background Checks on Violent Crime. Evidence that universal background checks may reduce total homicides is moderate, and evidence that such laws may reduce firearm homicides is limited. Evidence for the effects of dealer background checks on violent crime and total homicide rates is inconclusive. Dealer background checks have uncertain effects on violent crime and total homicides. Ludwig and Cook (2000) studied the impact of the 1994 Brady Act across states that had laws comparable with those that the Brady Act would impose (which initially included both background checks and a waiting period) and states that experienced larger changes in the law when the Brady Act was implemented.[⁠[2]](#fn2) They found uncertain effects of the policy on total homicides and firearm homicides and a suggestive decrease in nonfirearm homicides.
